platform: macOS 26.5 (25F71), arm64, Apple Silicon; debug build 08b291d with embedded frontend, WKWebView through the test bridge (src-tauri/src/test_bridge.rs)
harness: scripts/macos/m1-06-terminal-context.mjs (+ m1-05-terminal-lib.mjs) on scripts/macos/test-instance.mjs, bridge port 9443
method: One isolated instance on the pinned engine. Projects A and B under the proof's temp folder, one conversation each from the welcome screen, first message refused by the harness IPC guard (no turn). Terminal input through the panel's field (CDP Input.insertText of a whole line, real Enter; Ctrl+C as an AppKit key event). Add output to prompt and Run in Muse are clicked in the page. The composer question is inserted after the terminal block and sent with a real Enter. Replies are read from the stored transcript (muse-desktop.log.v1.<sid>) and the screen. The shell's ZDOTDIR points at a proof folder (one-line prompt), so the user's zsh files are not touched.

threadEntry.text:
$ echo RUN-IN-MUSE-MV6GO2WE
tool failed: environment failure: managed shell sandbox is unavailable
The execution environment is broken: the command was never started and every later command will fail the same way. Do not retry and do not fabricate command output; report this environment failure.

findings: Engine side, macOS: Run in Muse reaches the host (session/userShell accepted, the item and its text shown in the thread), but the command never runs: 'managed shell sandbox is unavailable'. m1-06-usershell-probe-macos.json reproduces it without the app, on the pinned 1.4.2 engine started from node with the app's flags: the Workspace and Network postures fail, only --disable-sandbox (the Elevated posture) runs the command. So it is not the app's spawn context. The 27/09 Windows reading of scripts/msp-user-shell-items.mjs ('markerEchoed: true') counts the marker inside the command text itself, so it cannot tell a run from a failure.
limits: Run in Muse output and a turn reading it are not proved on macOS (engine sandbox, above); the ticket's labelled-insertion path (Add output to prompt) carries the engine-reads-output criterion, as on Windows.
Terminal input inserted as whole lines (no smart-quote substitution; see M1-05 typed-quotes).
